issues.description: The problem statement asks students to implement a method named printFarmSong() in Farm.java, but the template and solution use a method named singFarmSong(). Additionally, the UML/spec expects a private singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) (or equivalent) that takes an Animal parameter, while the template's singFarmSongVerse currently has no parameter (commented out). This mismatch in method names and the missing parameter in the template will confuse students who look for printFarmSong and the expected verse signature described in the specification/UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the names and signatures across artifacts. Either update the problem statement to refer to singFarmSong() (and singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)) or change the template/solution method to printFarmSong() with the expected verse helper taking an Animal parameter. Also ensure the template's singFarmSongVerse signature includes the Animal parameter (e.g., singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)) so it matches the UML/spec and the solution.

issues.description: The problem statement (and UML/tasks) refer to a method named printFarmSong() to print/play the song, but both the template and the solution use the name singFarmSong() for the public method that performs this role. This mismatch between 'printFarmSong' (problem/task) and 'singFarmSong' (code) can confuse students when they try to map the task instructions to the provided code and when they search for the method to implement or call.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single, consistent method name across problem statement, template, and solution. Either rename the code methods singFarmSong() and any references to it to printFarmSong(), or update the problem statement and UML to refer to singFarmSong(), so the task instructions and starter/solution code match.
